text.p: French aluminium and packaging giant Pechiney announced planned job losses on Thursday and predicted that provisions for its "Challenge" cost-cutting plan would push the group into the red in 1996.

Chairman Jean-Pierre Rodier told a news conference the exact amount of provisions, which include costs of shedding up to 1,500 jobs in France, was not yet known but would include two billion francs ($388.9 million) in restructuring costs and result in a loss for the year.
"After provisions for Challenge, we will be in loss for 1996," he said. The provisions would only be known at the end of the year and then passed in the full-year accounts, he added.
Excluding the costs of the Challenge programme, full-year 1996 net earnings will be lower than the 732 million francs seen in 1995 on a proforma basis, the company said in a statement with results.
Pechiney reported first half net income fell to 426 million francs in the first half of 1996 from 658 million francs in the same period for 1995.
The Challenge plan has identified four billion francs in cost savings to be made by the end of 1998 and is Pechiney's bid to match the profitability of its best competitors.

Rodier said an important part of the savings would come from a 16 percent reduction in the total wage bill, with half of the savings to be found in France. The group employs 37,000 worldwide, of which 17,000 are in France.

The job reductions will come from up to 500 redundancies and 1,000 through early retirement. Use of flexible working would save 1,200 jobs, he said. The programme will avoid relocating plants abroad where costs are cheaper and will involve the closure of one French foundry which employs 72.

But labour organisations reacted angrily, with a joint statement from five trade unions denouncing the job losses as "unacceptable," while the CGT union in a separate statement called on employees to organise opposition to the programme.
Alongside the savings, about 3.5 billion francs will be invested in the next three years to modernise plants.

In the first half of 1996, Pechiney faced a worldwide reduction in demand from primary aluminium stemming from a sluggish European economy. But it benefited from lower financial expenses resulting from asset sales completed in 1995 and a capital boost that came along with its privatisation.

First half operating profit fell to 1.47 billion francs from 1.98 billion. Two-thirds of the decline came from the International Trade which had a strong performance in the first half 1995 and to changes in accounting for the Components and Systems division from consolidation to equity basis.
Weak demand and lower prices drove aluminium sales down 9.7 percent and operating profit down 17 percent.

In the packaging division sales rose 2.7 percent but profit was down 12 percent. Sales volume increased in Europe but declined slightly in the United States. Results for the North American operations were hurt by competitive pressure on prices.

In the Food, Healthcare and Beauty division, flexible packaging in the United States and the plastic tube business in Europe had a strong performance. But other activities, mostly in Europe had a stable to weaker performance.
The gearing ratio at end June 1996 was 89 percent against 85 percent at end December 1995.
Pechiney shares closed 0.70 francs lower at 213.30 francs before the profit figures and forecast were announced.
